title: Reading and writing: spelling from convertible words, the stress rule, written accents

cards.title: Use convertible words to read
cards.body: Unsure how a spelling sounds? Look at a convertible word you know: general shows ge = 'khe'; concentración shows ce = 'se'.

cards.title: The natural stress rule
cards.body: Words ending in a vowel, n or s (like most verb forms) are stressed on the second-to-last syllable: habla, hablan, importante. Words ending in any other consonant are stressed on the last syllable: comer, estar, salud.

cards.title: Written accent = the rule is broken
cards.body: A written accent only shows stress; it doesn't change the vowel sound (unlike French). Tradición ends in n but is stressed at the end, so it gets an accent.

cards.title: Accents that tell twins apart
cards.body: One-syllable words that look alike are distinguished by an accent: sí (yes) / si (if), mí (after prepositions) / mi (my), tú (you) / tu (your), sé (I know) / se.

cards.title: Question words take accents
cards.body: ¿Dónde estás? has an accent; donde in a non-question doesn't. Same with cómo (how) vs como (like). Many native speakers skip these too.

cards.title: Hook: the present tense
cards.body: Present-tense verbs end in a vowel, n or s and are stressed on the second-to-last syllable with no written accent; only estar breaks this (estás, está, están).

practice.why: Ends in n, stressed on the end → accent.
Ends in a vowel, stressed on the end → accent.
Ends in d → stress on the end, no accent.
